title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Finance and Bursary Administrator
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company

An exciting opportunity has arisen to join a highly regarded education and training organisation supporting the development of future professionals across the South West.

This organisation is known for its collaborative culture, commitment to personal development and supportive working environment, offering the opportunity to become part of a team that genuinely invests in its people.

Your new role

As a Finance & Bursary Administrator, you will play a key role in supporting both the financial and operational administration of a busy training programme.
You will be responsible for:
- Raising invoices and supporting day-to-day finance administration.
- Maintaining accurate financial records, spreadsheets and databases.
- Supporting funding and bursary administration processes.
- Assisting with payment schedules and reconciliations.
- Supporting trainee onboarding and record management.
- Administering trainee databases and ensuring information is maintained accurately.
- Responding to enquiries via telephone and email.
- Liaising with trainees, partner organisations and internal stakeholders.
- Supporting compliance, audit and reporting activities.
- Working closely with the Management Accountant and wider team.

This is a varied position combining finance administration, stakeholder engagement and programme support within a friendly and supportive environment.
What you'll need to succeedTo be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous finance administration, accounts administration or office administration experience.
- Strong customer service and stakeholder management skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Confidence maintaining accurate records and databases.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
- A positive, resilient and proactive approach.

Experience within finance, accounts payable, purchase ledger, business support, education administration or customer-focused administration would be highly advantageous, although full training will be provided on the specialist elements of the role.
What you'll get in return
- £16.75 per hour PAYE Premium or £18.93 per hour Umbrella.
- 37 hours per week.
- 33 days annual leave.
- Free onsite parking.
- Onsite café and excellent facilities.
- Friendly and supportive team environment.
- Ongoing mentoring and development.
- Exposure to a broad range of finance and administrative responsibilities.
- Initial contract expected until Christmas with the potential for extension and longer-term opportunities.

title: Administrator
description: At Sentinel Healthcare, delivering excellent patient care is at the heart of everything we do. We are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team, providing high-quality administrative and reception support across our clinical services. This varied and rewarding role involves supporting patients, clinicians and colleagues to ensure services run smoothly and efficiently. You will often be the first point of contact for patients, so a professional, compassionate and customer-focused approach is essential. The successful candidate will be organised, adaptable and able to manage multiple tasks in a busy environment. Excellent communication, attention to detail and strong IT skills are essential, along with the ability to work accurately and build positive relationships with patients, colleagues and partner organisations. We are looking for a supportive team player who is willing to work flexibly and contribute to a positive working environment. Previous experience in healthcare administration, particularly within primary or secondary care, would be advantageous. By joining Sentinel Healthcare, you will become part of a close-knit team that genuinely cares about making a difference to patients and the communities we serve. If you are looking for a rewarding role where your contribution is valued and every day brings something different, we would love to hear from you. Process electronic inbound referrals from GP's and other healthcare organisations using patient record systems. Booking and managing of patient appointments. Deal with routine patient enquiries. Ensure that electronic tasks are completed in a timely manner. Assist in monitoring generic email accounts. Send text reminder messages/emails to patients. Supporting Senior Administrative colleagues. Attending administrative and clinical meetings as required, which may occasionally be outside of core working hours. General office duties, such as post, scanning etc. Use the e-Referrals system (eRS) and the Electronic Patient Record systems (EMIS & SystmOne) to access inbound referrals and associated clinical documents booked in the Sentinel Healthcare clinical services. Liaise with local Referral Management Centres, GP surgeries and other external organisations as necessary. Using own judgement bring any GP referrals which may be inappropriate to the Clinician(s) attention. Ensure that inbound referrals are appropriately actioned i.e. accepted or rejected. Assist in co-ordinating the utilisation of booking slots across service areas, ensuring that capacity is fully utilised. Any under-utilisation to be reported promptly to the Operations Manager, so that appropriate action can be taken in advance. Re-book and cancel appointments as necessary in the patient record system and ERS. Any cancellations are to be undertaken following the set criteria for the service. Attention should be given to waiting time. Patients must be rebooked within specified time scales. Any problems meeting these criteria, including late cancellations, should be highlighted immediately to the Administration Manager. Ensure that relevant reminders (either by SMS, email or letter, where appropriate) have been sent to patients informing them of appointments. Ensure investigation requests are processed appropriately and results shown to the referring clinician. Assist in completing clinical coding and outcomes. Assist in using the patient record system to ensure that clinical reports and templates are re-produced and sent to GPs (and patients if required) following consultations. Open and prioritise correspondence, ensuring urgent correspondence receives prompt attention. Scan reports and other correspondence into the patient record system in a timely manner. Work closely with service area colleagues/clinicians to ensure good communication and that tasks are appropriately allocated and completed in a timely manner. Adherence to Sentinel Referral to Treatment Rulebook, Referral to Treatment Access Policy and to National Referral to Treat (RTT) waiting times rules and assist in making sure those targets are met. Assist in ensuring that Inter-Provider Transfer Forms (IPT) are completed and sent, as soon as the clinician requests onward referral to Secondary Care, in line with Waiting List Policy (48 working hours).
